answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: require each agent to stake a small deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can earn. A flood of new accounts then hits a real cost, like a gale against a stone wall, instead of free entry. Reputation should be earned in umber tones - slow, dark, cumulative - so a fresh copy cannot borrow the trust of an older one. And the ledger itself must stay sable-black transparent: every attestation public, every stake traceable, so sybil clusters stand out against honest agents.
